decisions.reason: The accepted solenoid-valve and station-button wiring coverage is already represented by the candidate's message-53 MODIFY.
The candidate's existing message-53 MODIFY already records the accepted solenoid valve and press-to-open, release-to-stop control behavior.
The candidate's existing message-53 MODIFY already requires the layout to represent the solenoid valve beneath the bowl in the button-controlled dispensing path.
The accepted dispensing-path consequences are already represented by the candidate's message-53 MODIFY, including the gravity-fed solenoid path and absence of retained matcha.
The accepted stainless-steel spout material is already represented by the candidate's message-53 INTRODUCE; the BOM additions require no further material-state change.
Adding solenoid-valve and button-control hardware does not necessarily change the existing requirement to minimize splashing.
The accepted dispensing hardware does not entail any change to the current base support or operational-stability requirements.
The candidate's existing message-53 MODIFY already records the accepted render-matched, custom-fabricated stainless-steel spout, and its RESUME resolves the prior scope ambiguity.
The solenoid and button-control additions do not alter the requirement that the bottom bowl seal prevent liquid from reaching the electronics.
The accepted hardware approach does not explicitly replace or narrow the existing requirement that the spout be removable or easy to flush.
Adding solenoid-valve and station-button hardware does not change the accepted 120V wall-power source or deferred battery-power decision.
